paths.description: Bare search.naver.com redirect and www.naver.com homepage, representing search entry, promotions, and JS resilience.
General query results plus autocomplete interaction, representing the primary end-to-end search task and result template.
Image vertical representing media-heavy result delivery and grid/card accessibility.

findings.summary: No system-driven dark theme
findings.evidence: Dark and default screenshots are byte-identical; all principal surfaces stay white under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces/text with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not reduce motion
findings.evidence: The default and reduce probes both report the same 300ms animation and 50 transitioning elements; loading-dot animations also remain defined.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential keyframes/transitions and stop auto-advancing motion.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference is not reflected
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot is visually unchanged while Lighthouse finds 23 low-contrast nodes, including tabs at 3.36:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors/forced-color-adjust where needed and raise text/control contrast under prefers-contrast and forced-colors.

findings.summary: State and route changes omit View Transitions
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules; the autocomplete interaction uses ordinary transitions and state replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance search state and same-origin result navigation with document.startViewTransition or cross-document view transitions, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long results do not expose scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The results page is over 5,300 CSS px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or equivalent position-aware chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/position affordance or responsive sticky search chrome using declarative scroll-state patterns.

findings.summary: Overlays use custom positioning rather than anchored primitives
findings.evidence: The DOM contains four custom role=dialog overlays, no popover elements, and no anchor-name/position-anchor/position-try CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for transient tooltips and menus.

findings.summary: Homepage interrupts content with browser-install promotion
findings.evidence: The initial homepage screenshot shows both a top install banner and a large floating Whale install panel obscuring the content before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the on-load panel or defer it until explicit interest; if retained, use a non-modal, easily dismissed disclosure.

findings.summary: Custom overlay semantics replace native primitives
findings.evidence: Results expose four role=dialog containers but zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover/details for transient/disclosure UI so focus, escape, and light-dismiss are platform managed.

findings.summary: Homepage chrome and promotions crowd the core task
findings.evidence: The first viewport devotes substantial area to install promotions, service icons, a large ad, and news chrome around the search field.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the search task and defer secondary promotions and dense service chrome below or behind explicit controls.

findings.summary: Desktop search response lacks a viewport contract and fixed-width layout overflows
findings.evidence: The desktop response has no viewport meta; layout measured 1,160px content in a 780px viewport with 380px overflow, and a 360px capture is scaled down rather than genuinely reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta tag and replace fixed minimum widths with intrinsic/fluid layout that reflows at narrow sizes.

findings.summary: Complex reused result components are not container-responsive
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules despite cards, AI panels, tabs, and side modules appearing in varied widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable modules containment and adapt internals with size/style container queries rather than page-wide fixed widths.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small or lose visible focus
findings.evidence: The active probe counted 58 controls under 44px in one dimension; several focused controls report outline:none, and Lighthouse confirms undersized 20px targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24px WCAG spacing and preferably 44px touch areas, plus a strong :focus-visible treatment for every control.

findings.summary: No-match search state presents unrelated commerce before clear recovery
findings.evidence: A deliberately nonsensical query immediately shows product ads/comparisons without a clear no-results explanation, query correction, or primary recovery action in the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Lead empty/low-confidence states with explicit status, spelling/query suggestions, and clear retry/edit controls before monetised fallback content.

findings.summary: Mobile search is far outside good Core Web Vitals
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 6.3s, LCP 30.5s, TBT 1,340ms, and performance 0.29; the desktop trace also measured LCP 4.45s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce critical JS/CSS, and defer non-essential result modules and telemetry until after interaction/idle.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout shift
findings.evidence: Layout evidence measured CLS 0.163 on desktop results and 0.769 on the redirected homepage mobile condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for async modules/promotions and stabilise image, font, and ad dimensions before content arrives.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace found four long tasks, longest 138ms, with 228ms TBT; mobile Lighthouse reported 1,340ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, schedule non-critical work by priority, and move independent computation off the main thread.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and render-blocking
findings.evidence: HAR captured 85 requests and 4.56MB transferred, including eight parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets and several high-priority scripts; trace LCP was 4.45s.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline/minimise critical CSS, defer non-critical styles and scripts, and tighten cache/compression policy.

findings.summary: Two megabyte-scale application bundles dominate the load
findings.evidence: HAR shows two separate index.js bundles at about 1.08MB each; scripts total 3.63MB across 41 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit coverage, deduplicate shared runtime/component code, split by result module, and load optional verticals only on demand.

findings.summary: Controls and images lack accessible names or valid semantics
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 14 images without alt, four unnamed links, one unnamed button, and three elements with disallowed aria-expanded; image search found 24 missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful alt or empty alt for decoration, accessible names for controls/links, and valid role/ARIA combinations.

findings.summary: Text and tabs fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 23 low-contrast nodes; search tabs use #8c8c8c on white at 3.36:1 instead of 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground contrast for tabs and metadata to WCAG AA across all states.

findings.summary: Landmarks, ARIA state, and focus treatment are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse found no main landmark and invalid ARIA; the focus probe shows the search input and multiple custom controls with outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic main/nav landmarks, valid roles/states, native controls, and consistent :focus-visible styling in DOM order.

findings.summary: Reflow and target sizing are not robust
findings.evidence: The desktop response omits viewport meta, scales a fixed-width page at 360px, and Lighthouse reports insufficient 20px touch targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Support 320px reflow/zoom without scaling the desktop canvas and enlarge or space all interactive targets.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling risks BFCache and platform compatibility
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports an unload event listener in nx-m-1.1.3.min.js, an API Chrome is removing.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange where needed and verify BFCache eligibility.

findings.summary: Search response has weak mobile/crawlability details
findings.evidence: The desktop result omits viewport meta, Lighthouse flags four generic “자세히 보기” links, and the search host intentionally blocks indexing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add viewport metadata to every variant and give links contextual accessible text; keep deliberate robots policy documented and consistent.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookies have avoidable gaps
findings.evidence: HTTPS and CSP are present, but HSTS and nosniff are absent; three first-party cookies lack Secure and all seven use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and nosniff, set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: The search load has a broad telemetry and cross-origin footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence saw 14 cross-origin hosts; HAR attributes 81/85 requests and 4.48MB to other origins, including logging, impression, and responsive telemetry endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory each data flow, remove redundant telemetry, batch required analytics, and delay it until consent/context where applicable.

findings.summary: Defensive browser headers are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers evidence confirms frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options, but no HSTS, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, nosniff, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; consider stronger script CSP/Trusted Types for the large app surface.

findings.summary: The redirected homepage is an empty JavaScript shell to non-JS clients
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 6% raw/rendered word coverage on www.naver.com with an empty #root; the crawler screenshot is effectively blank, while results reach 85%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the homepage core search, navigation, and essential content, then hydrate enhancements without making JS a prerequisite.

findings.summary: Image result delivery misses responsive and lazy-loading opportunities
findings.evidence: The images probe found 50 below-fold images without lazy loading and 48 images without srcset/responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images and provide responsive sources or equivalent negotiated sizing with efficient formats.

findings.summary: Large duplicate scripts and background telemetry waste device/network work
findings.evidence: Scripts transfer 3.63MB across 41 requests, including duplicate 1.08MB bundles, while several logging/impression calls run during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load result modules, deduplicate bundles, and defer/batch background analytics after the core task settles.

findings.summary: Cross-origin script and media cost is disproportionate for one result page
findings.evidence: HAR reports 4.48MB of 4.56MB from other origins, with large audio and image-viewer scripts loaded on a general result page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a per-template budget and only load audio, image-viewer, and other vertical code when the user opens those features.

findings.summary: Initial heap footprint is heavy for a search-results document
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 90.8MB self size, 1.45M heap nodes, 118,512 closures, and 13,265 FiberNode objects for about 3,049 live DOM elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicated bundles/component trees, virtualise offscreen modules, and release caches after result modules settle.

taskList.title: Cut LCP/TBT and duplicate JavaScript on mobile search
Restore responsive reflow, viewport handling, touch sizing, and visible focus
Fix accessible names, ARIA semantics, landmarks, alt text, and contrast
Reserve async/ad space to eliminate homepage and result CLS
Remove or defer the on-load Whale promotion and simplify homepage chrome
Complete HSTS, nosniff, Permissions-Policy, cookie, and data-minimisation controls
Server-render the homepage core search and navigation
Respect dark, reduced-motion, and high-contrast preferences
Use native dialog/popover and anchored positioning for overlays
Lazy-load and responsively deliver image results
Provide an honest no-match state before commerce fallback
Reduce the initial React/heap footprint and modernise unload handling
